title: Dynamic Calibration of Decision Thresholds for Financial Anomaly Detection: Verification With Payment Platform Information and Data
authors: Huang, A.; Zhang, X.; Wang, Y.; Tsai, S.; Zhou, P.; Chen, L.
tldr: A Temporal-Attention Isolation Forest with Dynamic Calibration (TA-IFDC) adaptively adjusts anomaly-score thresholds online and models inter-transaction temporal dependencies to detect payment fraud under distribution drift.
problem_and_motivation: Isolation Forest (IF) deployments in payment fraud detection rely on fixed anomaly-score thresholds that deteriorate when traffic shifts or is actively manipulated. Real payment traffic is non-stationary due to seasonal campaigns, macro shifts, and coordinated fraud rings. A robust, feedback-aware way to adjust cutoffs in unsupervised settings under streaming constraints remains underexplored.
approach: Sliding window preprocessing segments transaction streams into overlapping windows for online threshold adaptation.
Temporal attention encoder captures periodic patterns and behavior drift using Fourier-based positional encoding and scaled dot-product attention.
Isolation Forest scores each attention-enhanced transaction vector for unsupervised anomaly detection.
Dynamic threshold calibration module updates the decision boundary using a quantile-based smoothing rule blending historical and current score distributions.
Feedback-informed calibration optionally refines thresholds using delayed ground truth labels via false-positive and false-negative correction terms.
Evaluated on five payment datasets: IEEE-CIS, PaySim, CCFD, SFD-FD, and BankSim under streaming protocols with concept drift and delayed labels.
Benchmarked against six baselines: Online-iForest, Hybrid-AI, GNN-IF, XGB-Anomaly, SSR-RVFL, and autoencoder-based detector.
findings: num: TA-IFDC consistently outperforms all six baselines across five datasets in precision, recall, F1, and AUC.
num: Per-transaction latency stays within millisecond bounds, meeting real-time payment gateway requirements.
Ablation studies confirm that both dynamic calibration and temporal attention contribute independently to performance gains.
Dynamic thresholding maintains stable alert rates under induced concept drift conditions.
num: Quantile selection at 95th percentile balances precision and recall, with +/-1-2% guardrails under drift.
Delayed label feedback further refines threshold calibration without requiring frequent supervision.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a novel anomaly detection framework that treats threshold selection as an adaptive component rather than a static post-processing step. It demonstrates that combining temporal attention with dynamic threshold calibration addresses the gap between raw anomaly scoring and real-time decision-making in financial fraud detection. The extensive evaluation across five datasets establishes a comprehensive benchmark for streaming anomaly detection in payment systems.
directly_justifies: Dynamic threshold calibration enables IF to operate adaptively in non-stationary payment data environments.
Temporal attention module improves detection accuracy for sequential or contextual anomalies.
TA-IFDC consistently outperforms competitive baselines across multiple real and synthetic payment datasets.
limits: Evaluation limited to five specific datasets and six baselines; broader generalizability remains unverified.
Transformer-based detectors were excluded due to computational cost, leaving a comparison gap.
Real-world deployment at production scale with live traffic not demonstrated.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains found strong relevance in Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection), where the paper directly addresses anomaly detection algorithms and framework design. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) is relevant through the temporal dependency modeling component. Domain 4 (Landscape of Existing Systems) is relevant as the paper benchmarks against existing fraud detection approaches. Domains 1-3, 5, 7, 9-14 were considered but rejected as the paper does not address personal budgeting, user behavior profiling in personal finance, mobile-first design, or privacy concerns in personal finance systems. The paper is primarily an anomaly detection and fraud detection study rather than a personal finance management system.

limitations: Transformer-based detectors excluded from benchmarks due to GPU cost, potentially underestimating achievable performance.
Evaluation on synthetic datasets (PaySim, BankSim, SFD-FD) may not fully reflect real-world complexity.
No real-time deployment evaluation in a production payment system was conducted.
remember_this: TA-IFDC treats threshold selection as an adaptive component rather than a static post-processing step.
Dynamic calibration uses quantile-based smoothing with delayed feedback to track score distribution drift.
Temporal attention captures inter-transaction dependencies that pure IF scoring misses.
Extensive ablation confirms both calibration and temporal modules independently improve performance.
Framework maintains millisecond-level latency suitable for high-throughput payment gateways.
